title: Housing water grant, fleet funding and road tenders
subtitle: Brownfields tax increment phasing, capital project reclassification, Hillcrest and Quickfall reconstruction, and a restorative justice presentation.
overview: Council approved a short agenda of routine but significant spending items, each {{vote:m3}} unanimously in the case of the grant application. Staff were directed to apply to the Housing-Enabling Water Systems Fund for up to $35 million to support the Beaver Creek Road and Conservation Drive reconstruction, under the name Beaver Creek Meadows Infrastructure Expansion. If the application succeeds, the Mayor and Clerk may sign the grant agreement.

Council released $2,900,000 a year for fleet equipment replacement in 2024, 2025 and 2026 from the Equipment Reserve {{vote:m1}}. It awarded two road reconstruction tenders: Hillcrest Avenue {{vote:m4}} and Quickfall Drive and Langford Place {{vote:m6}}. It also reclassified eight capital projects as routine {{vote:m2}} and approved phased tax increment grants for the brownfield site at 119 Roger Street {{vote:m5}}.

The Quickfall project matters to families walking to Lincoln Heights school, since it includes wider sidewalks and changes at the school drop-off area. Council also heard from a community justice organization about restorative approaches to neighbour conflict. A councillor thanked by-law staff for St. Patrick's Day preparations. The meeting adjourned at 2:31 p.m.

decisions.detail: Staff will apply for up to $35 million in grant funding for the Beaver Creek Road and Conservation Drive reconstruction, and the Mayor and Clerk may sign the agreement if the application is successful.
Council released $2,900,000 from the Equipment Reserve for 2024 fleet replacement, with the same amount to be released on January 1 of 2025 and 2026.

decisions.item: Brownfield tax increment grant at 119 Roger Street
decisions.detail: Council approved phasing of the previously approved grant, with maximums of $728,954 for the initial registration phase, $392,820 for Phase One and $119,415 for Phase Two.

decisions.item: Quickfall Drive and Langford Place reconstruction tender
decisions.detail: The contract was awarded to Steed and Evans Limited for a total of $2,252,894.05 including unrecoverable HST.
The contract was awarded to 410754 Ontario Limited o/a Sousa Concrete for a total of $1,243,507.20 including unrecoverable HST.
Eight projects in the 2024-2026 capital budget, including Emerald Ash Borer management, urban forest management and the Affordable Housing Strategy, were reclassified as routine.

debate: On the water systems grant, one councillor asked whether the project could include innovations such as waste heat recovery from the sanitary system. Staff said low impact development features are being incorporated in design, but the narrow right-of-way limits other options.

On Quickfall Drive, a councillor asked how the project would improve safety for children walking and rolling to school. Staff said sidewalks will widen from 1.5 to 1.8 metres and the island in front of the school will shrink to give buses more room to turn and park.

Staff said students will be dropped off at a nearby church parking lot during construction. They said they would keep monitoring the street afterward with enforcement, transportation staff and the school board.

Delegates from a community justice organization urged Council to make restorative responses a first response to neighbour conflict rather than a last resort. They said by-law fines and police involvement can deepen disputes.

Councillors asked the delegates about mental health pressures, misinformation, and the difference between restorative and transformative justice. The delegates said mental health challenges do not rule out restorative approaches, and one councillor offered to meet them for further discussion.
